newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks break trend, end firmer.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks break trend, end firmer.

text.p: Breaking stride with a weeklong decline, Kuala Lumpur blue chips staged an afternoon rally to finish higher on Friday.
A late spurt in market heavyweight Telekom provided the fuel for the rise, a dealer said. "The market surprised us with the last-minute buying on Telekom," he said.

But main counters continued to lag secondary issues, which overcame profit-taking on Thursday to end up 1.13 percent. The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of the biggest 100 companies rose 8.08 points or 0.73 percent to 1,118.57, while the Second Board index added 6.02 points to 537.08.

"The Second Board is still quite active in terms of share price movement," said an analyst with a local research firm. "A big portion of the main board volume is from IPOs (initial public offerings)," he added.

One new listing that attracted interest on Friday was direct seller Amway, which surged from an offer price of 6.00 to as high as 14.70 ringgit before closing at 13.70. It traded over 9.3 million shares.
Stocks had a choppy session, with the Second Board index alternating between the plus and minus columns. Volume topped 180 million shares, versus over 220 million on Thursday.
